title: Sleep Problems in Parkinson's
content: Sleep problems are common among people with Parkinson's disease. Difficulties can include trouble falling asleep, waking frequently during the night, excessive daytime sleepiness, vivid dreams and movement or behavior during sleep. Parkinson's symptoms, medications, mood changes and other sleep disorders may contribute to disrupted sleep. Sleep difficulties can also occur for many reasons unrelated to Parkinson's disease. Persistent sleep problems or unusual movements or behaviors during sleep should be discussed with a healthcare professional.
